title: Dialysis Family Unable to Reach Hospital

fields.avatarBrief: woman in her sixties, wearing glasses and a cardigan, sitting in a living room with a phone in hand
fields.text: My husband got a call that his dialysis is moved to a clinic across town today but the van never showed and nobody at Ottawa River is answering the phone. He is 71 and in a wheelchair. His last treatment was Thursday. Is anybody else stuck?

comments.author: Tina R.
comments.text: This is terrible. I’ve tried calling the hospital three times since 8 a.m. and got no answer. I’m on the 6 a.m. shift and I can’t miss my treatment.

comments.author: Dr. Elena
comments.text: We have a transport team on standby. We’re checking in on all patients with rides. Please contact the HCC or the family reunification center if you haven’t heard from us.

comments.author: Critical Facilities Desk
comments.text: The hospital has not confirmed any transport failures. We are actively coordinating with community providers. Please do not share unverified information.

instructorNote: This is a misinformation inject. The family has not received a ride, but the hospital has not failed to coordinate. The CNO must activate the patient hotline immediately; the PIO must not engage the group directly.
